title: Preserves; Tool Handles; Composting
description: The premiere of Martha Stewart Living introduces Martha's philosophy of purposeful domesticity. She demonstrates how to make cherry preserves using a water-bath canning method, shows viewers how to paint tool handles in bright colors for easy identification, and explains the basics of starting a home compost pile from kitchen scraps.

title: Fishing Trip; Organizing Shoes; Cooking Fish; Pottery
description: Martha takes viewers on a fishing expedition and then shows how to scale and cook a fresh catch. She applies the same methodical approach to shoe storage, demonstrating a labeled box system, and talks about her collection of McCoy art pottery.

title: Flower Pots; Knot Herb Garden; Picnic Sandwiches
description: Martha designs an elegant knot herb garden using interlocking low hedges of different herb varieties. She also shows how to paint terracotta flower pots with a weathered verdigris finish and prepares layered picnic sandwiches designed to hold up without getting soggy.

title: Ribollita Soup; Herb Pots; Clothing Care; Tuscan Supper
description: Inspired by Tuscan farmhouse cooking, Martha makes a dense ribollita — the classic bread and bean soup thickened with leftover bread. She explains how to store woolens properly to prevent moth damage and fills a window box with culinary herbs for the kitchen.

title: Herb Brushes; Fiesta Ware; Tree Pruning; Grilling With Herbs
description: Martha bundles fresh rosemary and thyme into herb brushes for basting grilled meats, releasing aromatics as the brush applies marinade. She discusses her collection of vintage Fiesta Ware and demonstrates the proper season for pruning deciduous trees.

title: Halloween Party; Caramel Apples; Box Lantern; Cookies
description: An early Halloween episode establishes Martha's approach to the holiday: thoughtful decoration, homemade treats, and imaginative DIY projects. She dips apples in proper caramel, constructs a box lantern with a punched-tin pattern, and bakes shaped Halloween cookies with tinted icing.

title: Coconut Cake; Arranging Roses; Tag Sale
description: Martha bakes one of her most famous cakes — a towering coconut layer cake with shredded coconut pressed into white frosting — and discusses how she prepares for and runs a profitable tag sale. She also demonstrates arranging single-variety rose bouquets.

title: Making Pie; Felt Rounds; Sandblasting; Tool Kit; Bird House
description: A practical episode covering several domestic skills: perfecting a flaky pie crust, cutting felt rounds to protect stacked dishes, restoring furniture through sandblasting, assembling a well-stocked household tool kit, and building a simple birdhouse.

title: Thanksgiving Planning; Soufflés; Cran-Apples; Urns; Decor
description: Martha begins her two-week Thanksgiving sequence with advance planning strategies — what can be made days ahead, how to organize the refrigerator. She makes cranberry-stuffed baked apples as a side dish and demonstrates how to force soufflés in advance.

title: Thanksgiving Prep; Turkey; Stuffing; Gravy; Decorations
description: The full Thanksgiving episode walks viewers through Martha's complete holiday meal: a properly brined turkey, herb-and-bread stuffing baked inside the bird, velvety giblet gravy, and a table set with autumn foliage and dried seed heads.

title: Flavored Oils; Oiling Rusty Tools; Choosing Pots and Pans
description: Martha infuses bottles of olive oil with fresh herbs, dried chiles, and citrus peel as elegant homemade gifts. She also covers practical tool care — how to remove rust from garden implements — and explains what to look for when buying quality cookware.

title: Antiques; Scented Sugars; Rewiring a Lamp; Olive Bread
description: Martha layers flavored sugars with dried rose petals, lavender, and vanilla bean as pantry gifts. She rewires a vintage lamp on camera and bakes a rustic olive bread studded with Kalamata olives and fresh rosemary.

title: Christmas Wreath; Stockings; Christmas Brass Screw
description: The first Christmas episode focuses on fresh greenery. Martha assembles a classic boxwood wreath wired on a metal frame, sews personalized stockings from heavy wool, and explains proper care of brass fixtures and hardware.

title: Gingerbread House; Sugar Fruit Wreaths; Gift Wrapping
description: Martha constructs a detailed gingerbread house from scratch — baking flat panels from a royal icing-strengthened dough, assembling with piped icing mortar, and decorating with candy. She also makes sugar-frosted fruit wreaths and demonstrates her signature wrapped gift technique.

title: Building Fires; Candle Making; Miniature Topiaries; Brunch
description: A Christmas Day episode devoted to the pleasures of a winter home: how to properly lay and light a wood fire, dipping and finishing homemade taper candles, training small topiaries from ivy, and a complete holiday brunch menu.

title: Ribbons and Bows; Garden Cake; Grapefruit; Pantry Organizing
description: After the holidays, Martha turns to organizing — specifically the pantry, where she groups items in clear labeled containers and explains proper storage times. She also makes a cake decorated to look like a spring garden and demonstrates how to cut citrus supremes.

title: Hyacinths; Herb Garden; Knives; Natural Cleansers; Risotto
description: Martha forces hyacinth bulbs in glass vases so roots are visible and fragrant flowers emerge indoors in winter. She demonstrates proper knife sharpening with a whetstone and makes a classic risotto Milanese with saffron, stirring patiently through each addition of stock.

title: Chair Refinishing; Fruit Crumble; French Fries
description: Martha strips and refinishes a worn wooden chair, demonstrating how to apply stain evenly and when to use oil versus wax finish. In the kitchen she makes a fruit crumble with oat topping and prepares twice-cooked french fries with the proper soaking step.

title: Urban Archaeology; Chocolate Curls and Cakes; Potpourri
description: An episode covering antique hunting in New York City, where Martha demonstrates what to look for at flea markets. She shows how to shave chocolate curls with a vegetable peeler for cake decoration and makes a multi-layer chocolate cake with ganache.

title: Bottle Gardening; Wall Painting; Decorative Boxes
description: Martha plants terrariums and bottle gardens using small ferns, mosses, and selaginella. She also demonstrates decorative wall painting techniques — specifically a dragged finish — and shows how to line and cover decorative storage boxes.

title: Painting Porches; Country Breakfast; Opening Paint Cans
description: Martha repaints the floor and railings of a porch in her signature grey-green color, explaining surface preparation and proper brush care. She also makes a complete country breakfast: pancakes, fried eggs, home fries, and fresh squeezed juice.

title: Planting Roses; Valentine Chocolate; Pastry Bag
description: A Valentine's Day episode with practical romance: Martha explains bare-root rose planting — the best and most economical way to start a rose garden — and in the kitchen demonstrates proper pastry bag technique while making chocolate hearts and truffles.

title: Tomatoes; Raspberry Puree; Ice Cream; Dried Flowers
description: Martha covers tomatoes from seed to harvest, including which varieties to start from seed versus buy as transplants. She makes a bright raspberry coulis for desserts and a classic French vanilla ice cream churned from scratch.

title: Flavored Vinegars; Seed Starting; Ant-Free Pet Bowls
description: Martha steeps bottles of homemade herb and berry vinegars for salad dressings and marinades. She explains how to set up seed-starting trays under grow lights for early spring, and shares a simple tip for keeping ant-free pet food bowls.

title: Poppies; Salad Dressing; Tea; Madeleines
description: The proper vinaigrette gets demystified — emulsifying oil and acid in the right ratio with Dijon as binder. Martha makes madeleines, the shell-shaped French sponge cakes, in a specialized mold, and discusses how to brew a proper pot of tea.

title: Planting a Vegetable Garden; How To Cut a Mango
description: Spring planning for the kitchen garden: Martha lays out beds, explains crop rotation, and demonstrates direct seeding versus transplanting for different vegetables. She also shows the hedgehog method for cutting a mango cleanly without waste.

title: Growing Sweet Peas; Cutting Onions; Hors D'oeuvres
description: Sweet peas require early planting and support from the start — Martha explains timing and trellis setup. She demonstrates proper onion cutting technique (root intact to prevent tears) and prepares a tray of elegant passed hors d'oeuvres.

title: Peonies; Pasta; Staking Tomatoes
description: Martha's passion for peonies gets a full segment: planting, dividing, the importance of shallow depth, and care for blooms once cut. She makes fresh pasta by hand and demonstrates how to tie tomato plants to stakes without damaging the stems.

title: Easter Brunch; Tying Daffodils; Easter Baskets; Egg Hunt
description: A complete Easter episode covering both cooking and decoration. Martha prepares a pastel-toned brunch spread, ties daffodil bundles in garden twine, assembles natural Easter baskets filled with moss and decorated eggs, and designs an outdoor egg hunt.

title: Hydrangeas; Lobster Dinner; Mossy Pots; May Wine
description: The season finale celebrates the first warmth of spring. Martha makes a boiled lobster dinner with drawn butter and corn on the cob, explains how to grow hydrangeas in containers, coats terracotta pots with yogurt to encourage moss growth, and makes May wine — white wine infused with sweet woodruff.

title: Strawberry Pots; Shower Curtain; Succulents; Sugared Flowers
description: Martha opens Season 2 by making tiered strawberry planters from terracotta stacking pots, replacing a plastic shower curtain with a linen one finished with grommets, and showing how to dip fresh flowers and herbs in egg white and sugar for decorative edible garnishes.

title: Brick Edging; Shortcake; Ribbon Bulletin Board
description: Garden bed edges get a permanent solution with half-buried brick in a soldier course. Martha makes her classic strawberry shortcake with biscuits (not sponge cake) and mounts a ribbon-grid bulletin board for a home office.

title: Baked Apples; Mesh For Glass; Freezing Berries
description: Martha fills cored apples with brown sugar, butter, raisins, and spice before roasting them for a simple autumn dessert. She demonstrates a wire mesh technique for protecting glass surfaces and explains proper methods for freezing summer berries to preserve their texture.

title: French Toast; Rose Cutting; Sharpening Tools; Artichokes
description: Thick-cut brioche French toast soaked overnight in custard and pan-fried to a golden crust starts this episode. Martha shows how to take hardwood cuttings from rose bushes for propagation in autumn and how to properly steam artichokes.

title: Belgian Fence Espalier; Boning Chicken; Chicken Stock
description: Martha trains fruit trees in the classic Belgian fence espalier pattern — a diamond grid of angled branches — against a wall. In the kitchen, she demonstrates boning a whole chicken for stuffing and makes a proper long-simmered chicken stock.

title: Halloween Pumpkins; Cookies; Costumes; Decorating
description: Halloween gets the full Martha treatment: carved pumpkins with complex designs beyond standard faces, elaborately decorated sugar cookies in Halloween shapes, and creative costumes assembled from clothing rather than purchased kits.

title: Ribbon Lampshade; Rolled Linen; Photo Album; Video Boxes
description: Martha makes a lampshade wrapped with layered silk ribbon and demonstrates how to roll and store bed linens so they stay crisp. She shows how to organize photographs in an archival album and covers decorative video cassette storage boxes in marbled paper.

title: Apple Pie; Pie Dough In Box; Antiquing Urns; Brussels Sprouts
description: The American apple pie gets its definitive treatment: double crust, tart-sweet apple filling, and a lattice top crimped in Martha's style. She also explains how to store rolled pie dough in the refrigerator and shows how to antique cement garden urns with paint.

title: Cipollini Onions; DIY Chandelier; Squash Tartlets; Leaf Prints
description: Martha roasts cipollini onions — the small flat Italian variety — until caramelized for a side dish or antipasto. She makes a chandelier from a wire armature and candles and presses autumn leaves for nature prints.

title: Classic Thanksgiving Stuffing; Turkey, Gravy; Kitchen Decor
description: Martha's Thanksgiving issue comes to life on screen: a bread-and-herb stuffing made with day-old white bread and plenty of celery, a properly roasted turkey with crisp lacquered skin, and pan drippings reduced to silky gravy. The table is decorated with gourds and dried corn.

title: Potato Latkes; Silk and Velvet Scarves; Irish Oatmeal
description: Martha makes potato latkes — the Hanukkah fritters — properly grated and drained so they fry up crisp rather than steamy. She shows how to store and fold silk and velvet scarves without creasing and demonstrates how to cook steel-cut Irish oatmeal.

title: Christmas Cookie Ornaments; Trees; Stollen Bread
description: Cookie ornaments made from a no-spread sugar dough are hung on the tree with ribbon loops. Martha explains how to buy and care for a live Christmas tree, and bakes a traditional German stollen — the enriched bread with dried fruit and marzipan — for holiday gifting.

title: Christmas Ornaments; Wreaths; Cookie Boxes
description: Handmade glass ornaments get painted with etching cream for a frosted pattern. Martha constructs several wreath styles — boxwood, pinecone, and dried flower — and makes cookie-filled gift boxes lined with tissue paper and ribbon.

title: Gift Paper; Holiday Train Show Field Trip
description: Martha visits the New York Botanical Garden's Holiday Train Show, where model trains wind through elaborate miniature landscapes made from natural materials. She then demonstrates printing custom gift wrapping paper using carved potato stamps.

title: Winter Window Box; Chicken Stock; East Hampton House Tour
description: A Christmas Eve episode featuring Martha's East Hampton house decorated for the holidays. She explains how to plant a winter window box with evergreen cuttings and branches that will last through winter, and makes a clear golden chicken stock.

title: Silver Pouches; Caviar; Rolled Linens; Candles
description: New Year's entertaining gets the Martha treatment: caviar service with proper accompaniments, rolling and storing table linens to prevent creasing, and making organza pouches filled with silver metallic fabric for elegant party favors.

title: Sharpening Knives; Chicken Paillard and Orzo; Potpourri
description: Martha demonstrates sharpening knives on a whetstone — the proper angle, the pulling motion — and explains how to maintain an edge with a honing steel. She pounds chicken breasts into thin paillards for quick pan-cooking and serves them with orzo dressed in lemon and herbs.

title: Swiss Meringue; Transforming a Lamp; Hydrangea Wreaths
description: Martha makes Swiss meringue — beating egg whites over hot water before whipping — which is more stable than French meringue and ideal for frosting layer cakes. She rewires and transforms a dated lamp with a new shade and shows how to dry hydrangeas for long-lasting wreaths.

title: Forcing Bulbs; Book Covers; Fried Chicken
description: Paper-white narcissus bulbs are nested in pebbles and water to bloom indoors through winter — Martha explains timing for successive blooms through the season. She covers books in marbled paper and makes fried chicken with a seasoned buttermilk brine.

title: Coffee; Removing Lacquer; Decorating Cakes
description: Martha treats coffee as seriously as wine: proper storage, correct grinding, and brewing methods compared. She shows how to strip lacquer from brass hardware to return it to its natural patina and demonstrates cake-decorating techniques using a turntable.

title: Decorative Pastry; Clay Pots; Pie Kit Gift
description: Martha shows how to make decorative pastry elements — leaves, vines, and berries cut from dough scraps — for topping pies and galettes. She fills a basket with everything needed to make a pie as an assembled gift and shows how to restore old clay pots.

title: Fortune Cookies; Seven-Minute Frosting; Roses
description: For Valentine's Day, Martha makes fortune cookies with personalized messages tucked inside, demonstrates the glossy seven-minute frosting cooked over a double boiler until stiff peaks form, and explains how to properly condition cut roses to extend their vase life.

title: Wedding Bouquet; Turkey Hill House Tour
description: Martha shows viewers through her Turkey Hill property in Westport, Connecticut — the farm she made famous. She demonstrates assembling a hand-tied bridal bouquet of white garden roses and lily of the valley bound with satin ribbon.

title: City Bakery Field Trip; Seat Cover
description: Martha visits New York City's City Bakery to watch their pastry process — particularly their croissants and hot chocolate with homemade marshmallows. Back home, she upholsters a dining chair seat with new fabric and batting.

title: Espresso; Planting Trees
description: The Italian espresso tradition gets demystified: Martha explains the difference between espresso machines, how to tamp properly, and what makes crema. She also shows viewers how to plant balled-and-burlapped trees — proper hole preparation, backfilling, and staking.

title: Easter Lamb Cake; Easter Eggs
description: Martha bakes a lamb-shaped cake using a specialized two-piece mold, covering it in shredded coconut to mimic wool. She demonstrates natural egg dyeing using plant-based dyes — beet, turmeric, red cabbage — and traditional Ukrainian wax-resist decorating.

title: Rhubarb Crisp; Hanging Baskets; Iced Vodka; Vegetable Garden
description: Spring arrives in force: Martha harvests rhubarb for a crisp with oat and brown sugar topping, plants hanging baskets with trailing annuals, and infuses vodka in the freezer. She maps out the summer vegetable garden plan.

title: Asparagus; Trees as Gifts; Perennial Spring Border
description: Martha celebrates the short asparagus season — how to snap versus cut the stalks, how to store them standing in water, and preparations from simple roasted to asparagus soup. She explains planting a perennial border for sequential bloom.

title: Basic Herb Garden; Coffee Ice Cubes; Bamboo
description: An essential herb garden for the kitchen: Martha explains which herbs are annual and which perennial, how to position them for sun, and how to harvest without killing the plant. She makes coffee ice cubes for iced coffee that won't dilute.

title: Shade Garden; Lemon Granita; Irises
description: Martha closes Season 2 by designing a shaded garden using hostas, ferns, and astilbe that thrive without direct sun. She makes a lemon granita scraped repeatedly for a crystalline texture and discusses the art of iris breeding.

title: Pickling Green Tomatoes; Grilled Pizza
description: Martha preserves end-of-season green tomatoes in a spiced brine — one of the most distinctively American preserves. She also makes grilled pizza directly on the grill grate, explaining why the high heat produces a blistered crust impossible to replicate in a home oven.

title: Rosine Green; Making a Bed; Allied Down; Tulip Cutting
description: Martha demonstrates the right way to make a bed — tight hospital corners, precisely layered blankets — and discusses how to choose and care for down comforters. She explains tulip cutting: when to pick, how to condition, and how to keep them from drooping.

title: Teapot Shipping; Perennials; Lawn Aeration; Roasted Tomatoes
description: Martha shows how to safely pack and ship fragile objects like teapots. She walks through the fall perennial garden, explaining which plants to divide now for spring, and demonstrates roasting tomatoes slowly at low heat to concentrate their sweetness.

title: Seed Saving; Vanilla Whipped Cream; Planting Bulbs
description: Martha saves seeds from heirloom tomatoes, squash, and flowers for next year's garden — which ones to save versus buy, and proper drying and storage. She prepares vanilla-scented whipped cream and demonstrates spring bulb planting depths and spacing.

title: Scented Geraniums; Guacamole; Brush Cleaner; Glycerin Leaves
description: Scented geraniums — rose, lemon, nutmeg, mint — get a showcase: Martha uses them in cakes, teas, and sachets. She makes a proper guacamole from perfectly ripe avocados and preserves autumn leaves with glycerin for long-lasting decoration.

title: Gourd Lanterns; Doughnuts; Pumpkin Carving
description: Martha drills and carves dried gourds into hanging lanterns with star and crescent patterns. She fries fresh doughnuts — both glazed and old-fashioned cake style — and demonstrates pumpkin carving with a linoleum cutter for more detailed designs.

title: Autumn Gardens at Wave Hill; Propagating Ivy; Wood Care
description: Martha visits Wave Hill, the public garden overlooking the Hudson River in the Bronx, for a tour of its autumn plantings. She shows how to root ivy cuttings in water and covers the first of two segments on properly finishing and caring for wood furniture.

title: Wood Care Part 2; Roasted Garlic; Ginger Pumpkin Cake
description: The second wood care segment addresses polishing, oiling, and repairing minor scratches. Martha roasts entire heads of garlic until the cloves caramelize and can be squeezed out as a spread, and bakes a ginger-spiced pumpkin cake with brown sugar cream cheese frosting.

title: Marzipan; Cranberry Relish; Autumn Napkin Rings
description: Martha molds marzipan into realistic autumn fruits — tiny apples, pears, and squash painted with food coloring — as edible table decorations. She makes a raw cranberry relish with orange and ginger, and crafts napkin rings from autumn leaves laminated with glycerin.

title: Classic Thanksgiving Dinner: Turkey 101; Stuffing and Gravy
description: Martha's annual Thanksgiving episode gives viewers a comprehensive guide to the meal: properly preparing and roasting a turkey, making a bread stuffing fragrant with sage and thyme, and producing a smooth, lump-free gravy from pan drippings.

title: Pound Cake; Cold Frame; Hot Chocolate; Bean Bag; Gravlax
description: Martha builds a simple cold frame from old windows and lumber to extend the growing season into winter. She makes a classic pound cake, from-scratch hot chocolate with real cocoa, and demonstrates the curing method for gravlax — salmon salt-cured with dill.

title: Wreaths; Christmas Towel Stocking; Gingerbread House
description: The Christmas season begins early: Martha constructs several wreath styles including a pinecone wreath made from found materials. She creates a stocking from a vintage linen guest towel and assembles a gingerbread house with royal icing cement.

title: Holiday Decor: Tree Ornaments; Holiday Flowers; Lights
description: Martha's Christmas tree approach is naturalistic — glass ornaments in a single palette, dried orange slices, and pinecones. She explains how to arrange holiday flowers using forced amaryllis and paperwhites, and discusses different types of Christmas lights.

title: Pomegranate Sorbet; Decorations; Fruit Butter; Stockings
description: Martha makes a vivid magenta pomegranate sorbet and fruit butters — apple, pear, and quince — slow-cooked to a smooth spread for gifting. She sews Christmas stockings from velvet and trims them with silk ribbon.

title: Poached Pears; Tavern on the Green Christmas
description: Martha visits the legendary Tavern on the Green in Central Park during its Christmas decoration — an extravagant display of lights and ornaments. At home, she poaches pears in red wine with cinnamon and cloves for an elegant dessert.

title: New Year's Good Luck Meal
description: Martha explores New Year's food traditions from different cultures: collard greens and black-eyed peas from the American South, lentils from Italy, and round foods symbolizing coins. She makes a complete good-luck supper rooted in these traditions.

title: Chilies; Quesadillas; Coffee Can Toolkit; Arranging Flowers
description: Martha explores dried chili varieties — ancho, guajillo, pasilla — and makes quesadillas with homemade salsa verde. She assembles a compact toolkit in a coffee can as a gift idea and demonstrates loose asymmetrical flower arranging.

title: Puff Pastry; Palmiers; Cheese Straws; Ginger
description: Martha makes rough puff pastry from scratch using the quick method and rolls it into two classics: sweet palmiers dusted with sugar and savory cheese straws twisted from Parmesan-laced dough. A ginger syrup segment explores fresh ginger's applications.

title: Pruning Fruit Trees; Kindling; Special Kitchen Tools
description: January is the right month to prune dormant fruit trees — Martha explains heading cuts versus thinning cuts for apple and pear trees. She bundles kindling in neat bundles and gives viewers a tour of the specialized kitchen tools she uses most.

title: Chocolate Turnovers; Milk Paint
description: Martha makes chocolate turnovers using rough puff pastry and a dark chocolate filling — simple, satisfying, and bakery-quality. She demonstrates milk paint, a traditional American finish made from casein, which produces a flat, matte surface on furniture.

title: Artichoke Hearts; Poached Eggs; Eggs Benedict
description: Martha breaks down fresh artichokes to their hearts — trimming, rubbing with lemon, and storing in acidulated water — for use in pasta and salads. She poaches eggs perfectly in a gentle simmer and assembles classic eggs Benedict with hollandaise.

title: Chocolate Soufflés; Laminated Phone List; Greenwich Orchids
description: Martha tackles the chocolate soufflé with precise method: the base, the egg whites, the fold, the timing. She also visits a Greenwich orchid grower and explains how she maintains her large orchid collection, and demonstrates laminating documents without a machine.

title: Martha's Spring Garden Cake; Ivy Tips; Shoe Care
description: Martha bakes an elaborate garden-themed cake decorated with fondant flowers and a marzipan picket fence. She explains trimming and training ivy as a houseplant and gives a complete tutorial on caring for leather shoes — cleaning, conditioning, and storing properly.

title: Button Tacks; Seed Starting; Fruit Muffins; Forced Branches
description: Martha demonstrates making button tacks for upholstery, starts seeds under lights for spring transplants, bakes whole-grain fruit muffins, and forces spring branches — forsythia, quince, cherry — indoors in water for early blooms.

title: Spring Gardening: Clivia; Cleaning; Building a Cold Frame
description: The clivia lily, an underrated houseplant, gets its full showcase: how to get it to bloom, its preference for cool nights, and its remarkable longevity. Martha builds a cold frame from scratch and demonstrates a spring cleaning regimen for the household.

title: Easter Petit Fours; Baskets; Cookie Tree; Easter Egg Hunt
description: Martha makes pastel-colored petit fours glazed in a poured fondant coating for Easter. She creates elaborate Easter baskets from natural materials, builds a tree hung with decorated cookies, and designs a garden egg hunt.

title: Topiaries; Clematis; Staking Good Thing
description: Martha trains small topiaries in ivy and rosemary, explaining how to wrap wire frames and keep them trimmed. She covers clematis — the variety of climbing vines and how each requires different pruning — and shows a simple staking technique using twigs.

title: Pegging and Pruning Roses; Wreaths; Manure Tea
description: Martha teaches pegging roses — training long canes horizontally to encourage flowering along the entire length. She explains the concept of manure tea as a liquid fertilizer and makes a simple wreath from fresh garden cuttings.

title: Crab Boil; Spray Paint Furniture; Strawberry Lemonade
description: Martha makes a proper crab boil with Old Bay seasoning, steaming blue crabs at the table. She demonstrates spray painting metal outdoor furniture and makes fresh-squeezed strawberry lemonade from a strawberry simple syrup.

title: Angel Food Cake with Berries; Planting Urns; Brooklyn Garden
description: Season 3 closes with spring fully arrived. Martha bakes a proper angel food cake — whipped to a tall cylinder, cooled upside down — and tops it with macerated fresh berries. She plants terracotta urns with spring annuals and visits a remarkable Brooklyn garden.

title: Quesadillas; Hostas; Painted Lampshade
description: Martha opens Season 4 making quesadillas with homemade salsa and sour cream. She surveys her hosta collection — the extraordinary diversity of leaf color, size, and pattern — and shows how to paint a simple drum lampshade with a geometric stencil.

title: Composting 101; Compost Sifter; Homemade Mozzarella
description: Martha explains the composting process from the ground up: what to include, the carbon-to-nitrogen ratio, proper moisture, and when the compost is ready. She builds a simple compost sifter from hardware cloth and demonstrates fresh mozzarella pulled from hot curd.

title: Puerto Rico Part 1: Barrilitos Rum
description: The first of a two-part Puerto Rico field trip explores the island's traditions and ingredients. Martha visits a rum distillery to see the production of traditional Puerto Rican rum and learns about local cooking techniques from island cooks.

title: Sour Cherry Strudel; Garden Gloves
description: Martha makes sour cherry strudel using the paper-thin hand-stretched dough technique — a skill that requires practice and patience. She also discusses the range of garden gloves available and which tasks each type is best suited for.

title: The River Café; Lemon Tart; Stone Wall; Ribbon Box
description: Martha visits The River Café at the foot of the Brooklyn Bridge for a kitchen tour. She then makes an elegant lemon tart in a pâte sucrée shell with silky curd filling, demonstrates dry-stack stone wall construction, and covers a box in layered ribbon.

title: Apple Pizza Tart; Asters; Sunflower Wreath; Crème Fraîche
description: An unconventional apple tart is baked on pizza dough and topped with overlapping apple slices, creating a rustic pastry. Martha surveys asters in their fall glory, assembles a sunflower wreath with dried heads, and explains how to make crème fraîche at home.

title: Halloween: Scarecrow; Peanut Brittle; Window Creatures
description: Martha's Halloween episode moves beyond the expected: a scarecrow sewn and stuffed in elegant clothes, a perfectly pulled peanut brittle with baking soda added at the last moment for lightness, and window silhouette creatures cut from black paper.

title: Bread Pudding; Mattress Maker; Perfect Pot of Tea
description: Martha makes a custardy bread pudding from stale brioche with a whiskey sauce, visits a traditional mattress maker to understand construction and care, and demonstrates the British method for brewing the perfect pot of tea with properly preheated crockery.

title: Indian Food; Votive Jelly Jar Candles; Corn Garland
description: Martha explores Indian cooking in two parts, including tandoori techniques and spice blending. She makes simple votive candles poured into jelly jars with embedded wicks, and strings a corn garland using dried ears of multicolored Indian corn.

title: Raisin Pie; Cranberry Bog; Spiced Cranberry Mold
description: Martha makes a raisin sour cream pie — an old-fashioned American pie rarely seen today. She visits a cranberry bog at harvest to see the flooding and floating technique, then makes a jewel-bright cranberry mold for the Thanksgiving table.

title: Low-Country Thanksgiving: Deep-Fried Turkey
description: Martha explores Thanksgiving traditions from the American South's Low Country — deep-fried turkey in peanut oil (properly done in an outdoor fryer), she-crab soup, and cornbread dressing baked in a cast iron skillet.

title: Marshmallows; Rose Topiaries; Spiced Nuts; Hanukkah Candles
description: Martha makes homemade marshmallows — fluffy, vanilla-scented squares far better than any commercial version — and spiced mixed nuts as holiday gifts. She trains a rose topiary from a bare-root tree rose and shows how to make Hanukkah candles from beeswax.

title: Meringue; Pomander Gift; Felt Stockings
description: Martha shapes meringues into various forms — shells, kisses, and a vacherin ring — showing the technique's sculptural possibilities. She makes classic pomanders from oranges studded with cloves and cut-felt Christmas stockings with decorative appliqué.

title: Zuccotto Cake; Quilling; Paper Tree Skirt; Candlestick Wreaths
description: Martha makes a zuccotto — the Italian dome-shaped dessert of liqueur-soaked sponge filled with ricotta cream and chocolate — unmolded dramatically at the table. She demonstrates quilling (rolled paper strips) as a decorating technique and makes a tree skirt from paper.

title: Prime Rib 101; Yorkshire Pudding; Acorn Cookie Tree
description: A standing prime rib roast for the Christmas table gets the full Martha treatment: proper seasoning, high-heat start, roasting temperature, and resting time. Yorkshire pudding is made in the drippings alongside it. A cookie tree shaped from acorn-sized cookies closes the episode.

title: Puerto Rico Part 2: Plantains, Bananas
description: The second Puerto Rico installment explores the island's use of plantains and tropical fruits. Martha cooks with locals to learn tostones, mofongo, and banana desserts, and explores the culinary differences between ripe and unripe plantains.

title: Preserved Lemons; Yogurt Cheese; Opening a Coconut
description: Martha makes preserved Moroccan-style lemons — packed in salt and their own juice for weeks — an essential flavoring for tagines and salads. She strains yogurt into labneh (yogurt cheese) and shows the safest method for opening a whole coconut.

title: Wedding Cake 101; Wedding Good Things; Calla Lily Bouquet
description: Martha covers all aspects of wedding cake: the tiers, the dowels, the frosting techniques, and how a professional assembles multiple layers on site. She also demonstrates Good Things for weddings — small thoughtful details — and assembles a sleek calla lily bouquet.

title: Gnocchi; Cotton Wreath; Disney Topiaries
description: Martha makes potato gnocchi from scratch — the proper water content in the potato, how much flour to add, and the light touch needed. She visits Disney's topiary program to see their elaborate character-shaped plant sculptures and makes a cotton wreath from dried bolls.

title: Drop Biscuits; Hyman Hendler; Trimming Pillowcases; Tapenade
description: Drop biscuits — the simpler, no-rolling version — get the same attention as their rolled cousins. Martha visits Hyman Hendler's ribbon showroom in New York, trims pillowcases with embroidery and ribbon, and makes tapenade from a mix of olives and capers.

title: Black Bass; Sea Urchins; Compound Butters
description: Martha cooks black sea bass whole in the oven with fennel and tomatoes and explains how to eat sea urchin — the prized roe consumed raw. She makes a series of compound butters: anchovy, tarragon, blue cheese, and citrus, for finishing sauces and grilled meats.

title: Tempering Chocolate; Coeur à la Crème
description: Tempering chocolate on a marble slab — the technique that gives dipped candies and decorations their snap and sheen — gets a full demonstration. Martha makes coeur à la crème for Valentine's Day, the heart-shaped cream cheese dessert unmolded onto a plate of berry coulis.

title: Chocolate Chip Angel Food Cake; Manhattan Fruitier
description: Martha folds mini chocolate chips into angel food cake batter for a variation on the classic. She visits The Manhattan Fruitier, whose elaborate gift baskets of exotic fruits are beloved in New York, and examines the logic behind seasonal fruit pairing.

title: Gardening: Planting and Propagating Tomatoes; Beekeeping
description: Early planning for tomato season: Martha explains how to read seed catalogs, start seeds under lights, and eventually harden off seedlings. She also shows the beekeeping work on her property — managing hives, extracting honey, and protecting bees from disease.

title: Ham 101; Chocolate Eggs and Nests; Decorating Easter Cookies
description: Martha roasts a bone-in ham with a brown sugar and mustard glaze for Easter. She makes hollow chocolate Easter eggs poured into molds and constructs shredded-wheat nests filled with candy eggs. Decorated Easter cookies are piped in pastel royal icing.

title: Begonias; Ground Covers; Moss Container; Hot Fudge
description: Martha explores tuberous begonias — starting from tubers, the watering requirements, and achieving their large dramatic blooms. She plants a moss-covered container garden and makes a proper hot fudge sauce that stays fluid over ice cream without seizing.

title: Victorian Rose Bouquet; Cocoa Sorbet; Fern Napkins
description: Martha creates a tightly packed Victorian-style rose bouquet in a collar of fern fronds. She makes a dark, intense cocoa sorbet using Dutch-process cocoa and demonstrates how to fold fabric napkins into decorative shapes for formal table settings.

title: Grill Basics; Grilling Seafood; Salsa and Shrimp
description: Memorial Day grilling: Martha covers charcoal selection, fire starting without lighter fluid, and temperature control. She grills whole fish, large shrimp skewered with herbs, and makes a fresh salsa verde to serve alongside.

title: Bare Root Roses; Daffodil Bundles; Container Garden
description: Bare root roses offer the best selection and value in spring — Martha explains soaking the roots, proper planting depth, and initial pruning. She ties large bundles of daffodils with raffia for arrangements and plants a container garden with annuals.

title: Daylilies; Scallops; Ice Cream Sandwiches
description: Season 4 closes in early summer. Martha surveys her daylily collection at peak bloom — the remarkable variety of color and form in modern hybrids. She sears scallops until golden-crusted, and makes homemade ice cream sandwiches with chocolate chip cookies and vanilla ice cream.
